subject: Re: March ingestion spike — proposed credit split and VAT handling
messages:
From: Elena Kovac <elena.kovac@clearlens.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@clearlens.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: March spike adjustment + VAT evidence

Hi Vivek,

We noticed a large ingestion spike during the weekend of Feb 26–28 that caused our March invoice to be ~28% higher than forecasted. Our engineering team confirmed the spike was caused by a misconfigured connector from a partner; this was transient and outside normal usage.

Can Redwood provide a remediation path? Ideally: a goodwill credit for the unexpected overage and a short note we can include in our VAT filing that explains the adjustment (we are EU-registered). Our accounting team needs: credit amount, whether the credit will be issued as a negative invoice or a service credit, and any supporting docs showing the dates/usage buckets.

We are under a quarterly budget review this week; if we can get a proposal by EOD Wed (Mar 3) it helps us close Q1 numbers.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if easier.

Best,
Elena Kovac
Finance Manager, ClearLens Inc.
Attachment: spike-summary.csv (usage CSV)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: March spike adjustment + VAT evidence

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding ClearLens request. Snapshot below.

Quick thoughts:
- Recommend a two-part remediation: (1) a one-time goodwill credit to cover 100% of the overage that is attributable to the Feb 26–28 spike (amount TBD), and (2) reissue a corrected invoice for March that nets the credit for their records.
- For EU VAT: we should provide an explanatory credit memo (PDF) that they can attach to their VAT submission. Finance will need GL codes and whether this is a refund/credit memo or account-level service credit.
- Risk/precedent: give full goodwill this one time but record as a non-recurring customer concession. We'll flag in CRM (deal DL-21987).

Marissa, can you:
  1) Confirm whether we issue a negative invoice or an account-level service credit from an accounting perspective (and any downstream tax implications).
  2) Draft a short credit memo text that explains the dates, usage buckets, and that the adjustment is corrective for an ingestion anomaly.
  3) If possible, produce a pro forma credit schedule so we can send Elena numbers tomorrow morning.

Karthik — will you confirm commercial approval? My recommendation is no discount to future usage, just courtesy remediation.

Attaching: proposed-credit-plan.xlsx (staging worksheet)

— Vivek
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: March spike adjustment + VAT evidence

Vivek / Karthik — accounting notes below.

1) Mechanism: we should issue a credit memo (negative invoice) tied to the original March invoice. That provides ClearLens with a standalone document they can include with VAT filings.
2) Tax/VAT handling: because ClearLens is EU-registered and the spike is corrective (not a contract change), we will mark the credit as: "service credit — corrective adjustment" and include dates and usage buckets. This allows them to offset VAT as appropriate; they should consult their tax advisor but this is standard practice.
3) GL treatment: use GL code 5402 (Customer concessions) and tag as non-recurring adjustment in ledger.
4) Withholding/TDs: Not applicable for EU–EU customer, but if they request a refund to an Indian entity or with an Indian tax treaty, we'll need additional forms.

I drafted the credit memo PDF and attached a fill-in template: CreditMemoDraft.pdf. I also prepared the numbers in the worksheet Vivek attached — you'll see a highlighted row with the proposed credit amount: EUR 12,450 (100% of overage).

If everyone signs off I can:
- Generate the official negative invoice/credit memo and route to DocuSign (we can have ClearLens sign acknowledgement)
- Flag the CRM record with concession code "GOODWILL_1TIME"

Karthik — commercial ok?

Cheers,
Marissa
Attachment: CreditMemoDraft.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kovac <elena.kovac@clearlens.com>, ClearLens Finance <finance@clearlens.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: March ingestion spike — proposed credit split and VAT handling

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the CSV. We investigated on our side and can confirm the spike was transient (partner connector misconfig) and outside normal usage patterns. We propose the following remediation: 

Summary proposal (one-time):
- Goodwill credit: EUR 12,450 (100% of the identified overage for Feb 26–28).
- Mechanism: Redwood will issue a negative invoice (credit memo) dated Mar 3, 2027 referencing the original March invoice number. This will appear as a separate document you can attach to VAT filings.
- Supporting evidence: we'll provide (a) usage bucket snapshot (CSV), (b) the credit memo PDF, and (c) an internal note describing the cause/date-range.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Finance sign-off: Marissa to produce and send credit memo for signature — target EOD Wed Mar 3 (attached draft).
2) You acknowledge and sign the credit memo via DocuSign (link to follow).
3) Once signed we will post the credit to your account and reissue the net invoice.

Please confirm you’re comfortable with the amount and mechanism. If you prefer the credit applied as an account-level offset instead of a negative invoice, let us know — we can do either, but a credit memo is easiest for VAT traceability.

Thanks — sorry for the disruption and happy to join a short call if helpful.

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
viv e k@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
